# 1 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_005_page_001.jpg

---

1. When the Gentiles all around heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary rededicated as it was before, they were greatly enraged.
2. They plotted to destroy the descendants of Jacob who lived among them, and they began a campaign of slaughter and elimination among the people.
3. Judas made war against the Idumeans in Akrabattene, because they were harassing Israel; he struck them with a great blow, humbled them, and took their plunder.
4. He also remembered the malice of the sons of Baean, who had been a trap and a snare to the people, lying in wait for them on the roads.
5. He besieged them in their towers, encamped against them, put them under the ban, and burned their towers with fire along with everyone inside.
6. Then he crossed over to the Ammonites, where he found a large and powerful force with Timothy at their head.
7. He fought many battles against them; they were routed before him, and he crushed them.
8. He seized Jazer and its dependent villages, then turned back toward Judea.
9. Meanwhile the Gentiles in Gilead gathered against the Israelites who lived in their territory to destroy them; those Israelites fled to the fortified stronghold of Dathema.
10. They sent a letter to Judas and his brothers saying: "The Gentiles around us have gathered against us to destroy us.
11. They are preparing to come and seize the stronghold to which we have fled, and Timothy is leading their forces.
12. Come now and rescue us from their hands, for many of us have already fallen.
13. All our kindred in the land of Tobias have been killed; the enemy has taken captive their wives and children and their property, killing about a thousand people there."
14. While they were still reading this letter, other messengers arrived from Galilee with their garments torn, bringing a similar report.
15. They said: "The people of Ptolemais, Tyre, and Sidon have joined with all the Gentiles of Galilee to destroy us."
16. When Judas and the people heard this, a great assembly was convened to decide what should be done for these kinsmen who were in distress and being attacked by enemies.
17. Judas said to his brother Simon: "Choose your men and go and rescue your kindred in Galilee. My brother Jonathan and I will go to Gilead."
18. He left Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah in command of the people, with the remaining forces, to hold Judea;
19. and he gave them these orders: "Take charge of this people, but do not engage the Gentiles in battle until we return."
20. Three thousand men were assigned to Simon for the campaign in Galilee, and eight thousand to Judas for Gilead.
21. Simon went into Galilee and fought many battles against the Gentiles. The Gentiles were routed before him,
22. and he pursued them to the very gate of Ptolemais. About three thousand Gentiles fell; he took their plunder.
23. He then gathered the Jews who were in Galilee and in Arbatta, with their wives and children and everything they possessed, and brought them back to Judea with great rejoicing.
24. Judas Maccabeus and his brother Jonathan crossed the Jordan and marched three days through the wilderness.
25. The Nabateans met them and welcomed them peaceably, reporting to them everything that had happened to their kindred in Gilead:
26. that many of them were shut up in Bosora, Bosor in Alema, Caspho, Maked, and Carnaim — all large, well-fortified cities —
27. and that others were confined in the remaining cities of Gilead, and that the enemy planned to attack the strongholds on the following day, seize them, and destroy all the men in a single day.
28. At once Judas turned his army and marched by the desert road to Bosora. He took the city, put all the men to the sword, seized all the plunder, and burned the city.
29. They moved out by night and traveled until they reached the stronghold.
30. At dawn, when they looked ahead, they saw an enormous force — beyond counting — carrying ladders and siege engines to capture the stronghold, and already fighting the garrison.
31. Judas saw that the battle had been joined, and that the cries of the city rose to heaven along with trumpets and a great din.
32. He said to his men: "Fight for your kindred today!"
33. He led three companies in a charge against the enemy's rear, sounding trumpets and crying out in prayer.
34. When the army of Timothy recognized that it was Maccabeus, they fled before him; he struck them a great blow. About eight thousand of them fell that day.
35. He then wheeled against Maspha, attacked it, took it, killed all the males, seized the plunder, and burned it.
36. From there he marched and took Caspho, Maked, Bosor, and the other cities of Gilead.
37. After these events Timothy assembled another army and camped opposite Raphon on the far side of the ravine.
38. Judas sent scouts to reconnoiter the army. They returned with a report: "All the nations around us have gathered to him — it is a very large force.
39. They have also hired Arab auxiliaries; they are camped on the far side of the ravine, ready to advance against you and fight." And Judas went to meet them.
40. Timothy said to the commanders of his force: "If Judas crosses the ravine to engage us first, we will not be able to withstand him — he will certainly overpower us.
41. But if he holds back and camps on the other side, we will cross over and overpower him."
42. As Judas approached the ravine, he stationed the officers of the army at the bank and issued orders: "Let no one hold back; everyone must advance to battle."
43. He himself crossed over first, and all the people followed. The Gentiles were routed before them, threw away their weapons, and fled to the temple precinct at Carnaim.
44. They took the city and set fire to the temple precinct with everyone in it. Carnaim was subdued and could hold out no longer against Judas.
45. Judas mustered all the Israelites who were in Gilead — young and old, with their wives, their children, and all their belongings — a very great company, to journey to the land of Judah.
46. They came to Ephron, a large city lying across their path, powerfully fortified; there was no way to bypass it, either right or left — they would have to go through it.
47. The people of the city locked them out and barricaded the gates with stones.
48. Judas sent them a message of peace: "Let us pass through your land to reach our own land. No one will harm you; we will simply pass through on foot." But they refused to open.
49. Judas then gave the order throughout the camp for everyone to halt and set up camp where he stood.
50. The soldiers encamped there and fought against the city all that day and all that night; the city fell into his hands.
51. He put all the males to the sword, leveled the city to its foundations, seized the plunder, and marched through the city over the bodies of the slain.
52. They crossed the Jordan into the great plain before Beth-shan.
53. Throughout the march Judas kept gathering the stragglers and encouraging the people, until they arrived in the land of Judah.
54. They went up to Mount Zion with joy and gladness and offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen before they returned home safely.
55. Now while Judas and Jonathan were in Gilead and Simon his brother was in Galilee before Ptolemais,
56. Joseph son of Zechariah and Azariah, the commanders of the forces, heard of the brave deeds and the battles the others had won.
57. They said: "Let us also win renown by going out to fight the Gentiles around us."
58. They issued orders to their troops and marched toward Jamnia.
59. But Gorgias and his men came out of the city to engage them in battle.
60. Joseph and Azariah were routed and pursued to the borders of Judea. About two thousand Israelites fell that day.
61. It was a great defeat for the people, because the commanders had not listened to Judas and his brothers and had acted on their own initiative.
62. They were not of the stock of those men through whose hands deliverance had been given to Israel.
63. The man Judas and his brothers were greatly honored throughout all Israel and among all the Gentiles, wherever their name became known.
64. People thronged to them and praised them.
65. Judas then marched with his brothers against the Idumeans in the Negeb. He struck Hebron and its surrounding villages, tore down its strongholds, and burned the towers around it.
66. He moved camp and marched into Philistine territory, passing through Marissa.
67. On that day some priests who were eager to win honor fell in battle; they had gone out to fight without authorization.
68. Judas turned aside toward Azotus in Philistine territory; he tore down their altars, burned the carved images of their gods, plundered their cities, and returned to the land of Judah.
